chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Ja'far ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When you hear him reciting poetry in the mosques, say: May Allah open your mouth [in mockery/ridicule], for the mosques were established only for the Quran.'

key_terms.فَضَّ اللَّهُ فَاكَ: May Allah open your mouth (a phrase of mild ridicule or emphasis)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on reciting poetry in mosques according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration to define the sanctity of mosques as spaces exclusively dedicated to the remembrance of God and the Quran, distinguishing them from general public venues. The specific instruction to say 'May Allah expose your mouth' (a mild rebuke) reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on preserving the spiritual atmosphere of the mosque from distractions like poetry recitation, which, while valid elsewhere, detracts from the primary act of *dhikr* and Quranic study.
